stem: A 45-year-old woman presents to clinic with 8 weeks of bilateral symmetric polyarthritis involving the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints, proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints, and wrists. She reports >2 hours of morning stiffness that improves with activity. Exam shows synovitis (boggy, tender, mildly swollen) of multiple MCP and PIP joints and both wrists; the distal interphalangeal joints are spared. There is no skin rash, no nail pitting, no sicca symptoms, no preceding gastrointestinal or genitourinary infection, no Raynaud phenomenon. Labs: rheumatoid factor 80 IU/mL (positive); anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody (anti-CCP) 250 U/mL (markedly positive); ESR 65 mm/h, CRP 32 mg/L. Hand and wrist X-rays show marginal erosions of several MCP joints and periarticular osteopenia. ANA negative; CBC normal.
question: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis per the 2010 ACR/EULAR Classification Criteria (joint involvement + high-titer serology + elevated acute-phase reactants + duration ≥6 weeks)
options.D: Inflammatory arthritis not yet meeting RA classification criteria; arrange close watchful follow-up with serial assessment

rationale: The 2010 ACR/EULAR Classification Criteria for RA require a score of ≥6/10 across four domains: (1) joint involvement (1 large = 0, 2–10 large = 1, 1–3 small = 2, 4–10 small = 3, >10 with at least 1 small = 5); (2) serology (negative = 0, low-positive RF or anti-CCP = 2, high-positive = 3); (3) acute-phase reactants (normal = 0, abnormal CRP or ESR = 1); (4) symptom duration (<6 weeks = 0, ≥6 weeks = 1). This patient's score: 4–10 small joints (3) + high-positive serology (3) + abnormal acute phase (1) + duration ≥6 weeks (1) = 8/10 → meets RA classification. Erosive disease on imaging supports the diagnosis. SLE (option B) is excluded by the absence of typical SLE features (no rash, no oral ulcers, no serositis, no cytopenias) and the negative ANA. Psoriatic arthritis (option C) is excluded by the absence of skin/nail psoriasis and DIP joint involvement. Inflammatory arthritis not meeting criteria (option D) is reserved for patients who do not yet score ≥6 — this patient does score ≥6.

variants.stem_override: A 65-year-old man presents to clinic with 10 weeks of bilateral symmetric polyarthritis involving the MCP, PIP, and wrist joints with >2 hours of morning stiffness. Exam shows synovitis of multiple MCP and PIP joints and both wrists; DIPs are spared. No skin rash, no preceding infection. Labs: rheumatoid factor NEGATIVE; anti-CCP NEGATIVE; ESR 60 mm/h, CRP 30 mg/L. Hand and wrist X-rays show marginal erosions of several MCP joints. ANA negative.
variants.rationale_for_variant: Sex / age perturbation with seronegativity. The 2010 ACR/EULAR score is: 4–10 small joints (3) + serology negative (0) + abnormal acute phase (1) + duration ≥6 weeks (1) = 5/10 — JUST BELOW the ≥6 threshold for definite RA classification. However, the presence of erosive disease on imaging and the bilateral symmetric small-joint synovitis strongly support clinical RA (the classification criteria are intentionally conservative; many clinically definite seronegative RA patients score 5/10). Most rheumatologists would still treat this patient as RA. To be clinically defensible, the appropriate label here is 'inflammatory arthritis not yet meeting strict 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria (5/10) — but with high clinical suspicion for seronegative RA with erosive disease, watchful follow-up and consideration of early DMARD'. The correct answer therefore shifts to option D.

variants.stem_override: A 40-year-old woman presents to clinic with 2 weeks of bilateral hand and wrist arthralgia (joint PAIN without exam evidence of synovitis) and 30 minutes of morning stiffness. Exam shows mild MCP and wrist tenderness without boggy swelling, warmth, or limitation of motion. There is no skin rash, no preceding infection, no other systemic features. Labs: rheumatoid factor NEGATIVE; anti-CCP NEGATIVE; ESR 18 mm/h (normal), CRP 4 mg/L (normal). Hand X-rays are normal with no erosions or osteopenia.
variants.rationale_for_variant: Pure demographic with very early symptoms — but the clinical picture does NOT meet 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria: there is no exam-confirmed synovitis (the criteria require active synovitis on examination, not arthralgia alone), the duration is <6 weeks, the serology is negative, and the acute-phase reactants are normal. Score: 0 (no synovitis) + 0 (negative) + 0 (normal) + 0 (<6 weeks) = 0/10. This is ARTHRALGIA, not yet inflammatory arthritis. The appropriate approach is watchful follow-up with re-examination at 6–12 weeks, repeat serologies if symptoms progress or worsen, and reassessment for evolving synovitis. The correct answer therefore is option D.

sources: Aletaha D et al. 2010 Rheumatoid Arthritis Classification Criteria: an American College of Rheumatology / European League Against Rheumatism collaborative initiative. Arthritis Rheum 2010;62:2569-2581.
van der Linden MPM et al. Classification of rheumatoid arthritis: comparison of the 1987 ACR and 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria. Arthritis Rheum 2011;63:37-42.
Smolen JS et al. EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2022 update. Ann Rheum Dis 2023;82:3-18.
